title: uart: reading the current line-break status
conditions: While the UART receiver is enabled and the RX line is, or has been, held low long enough to count as a break (CTRL.RXBLVL character times).
Each setting is encoded as 1 if the statement about the design holds and 0 if it does not.

requirements.text: The `rx_break_err` interrupt is triggered if a break condition has been detected.
Note that only one interrupt is generated per break -- the line must return high for at least half a bit-time before an additional break interrupt is generated.
The current break status can be read from the [`STATUS.BREAK`](registers.md#status) bit.
If STATUS.BREAK is set but [`INTR_STATE.BREAK`](registers.md#intr_state) is clear then the line break has already caused an interrupt that has been cleared but the line break is still going on.
requirements.note: Line 161 describes the opposite combination with the same two names.

design.description: no register field or interrupt named BREAK (the break detection level values are break2 to break16)
no STATUS field is driven from the break detector

design.note: The last of STATUS's six fields: TXFULL, RXFULL, TXEMPTY, TXIDLE, RXIDLE and RXEMPTY. The core drives exactly these six (uart_core.sv lines 148 to 153).
The interrupt, and so the INTR_STATE field, is named rx_break_err.
The break event drives the rx_break_err interrupt.
A break event is raised only in state BRK_CHK; the event moves the detector to BRK_WAIT (line 130).
The detector returns to BRK_CHK only when the RX input is high. The state break_st_q (line 96) is internal: it reaches no register.

claims.setting: a detected break raises an interrupt (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: agrees

claims.setting: after a break interrupt, no further one until the RX line has been high (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: agrees

claims.setting: software can read the current break status from a STATUS bit (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: disagrees

claims.setting: INTR_STATE has a field named BREAK (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: disagrees

generated_from_same_input: D1, D3 and D4 are in uart.hjson, from which reggen generates the register RTL and registers.md; those generated files are not counted as further evidence. D2 and D5 to D7 are in the hand-written uart_core.sv. R1 to R4 are hand-written.
finding: The interrupt and its one-per-break behavior agree with the design (C1, C2). R3 tells software to read the current break status from STATUS.BREAK, and R4 and line 161 explain how to combine it with INTR_STATE.BREAK. The design has neither: STATUS has six FIFO and idle fields and none for break, the core keeps the break state in an internal register that reaches no register, and the interrupt field is rx_break_err. Software that follows R3 reads a bit that does not exist; the only break indication available is the rx_break_err interrupt.
missing_information: This case reads the register description and the core's break detector; it does not simulate a break. The "half a bit-time" in R2 depends on how the receiver samples rx_in and is not checked.
ambiguities: R4 and line 161 could be read as describing INTR_STATE.rx_break_err under a shorter name. Even so, they depend on STATUS.BREAK, which has no counterpart.
out_of_scope: How a top-level design connects the RX pin or its pull resistors, which R1's section also discusses.
